analysis.investment_thesis: Can Fin Homes is a conservatively run housing finance company with decent ROE (16.9%), attractive valuations (P/E 11.9x, forward P/E 10.5x), and solid 22% net profit CAGR — but the PSU-bank promoter at only 30% holding, rising finance costs, and the inherent leverage of an HFC (D/E 6.59x) means this does not meet my standards for a quality financial services compounder.
key_strengths: Affordable housing focus with 22.1% net profit CAGR over 3 years and ROE of 16.9% — operationally a decent business
Valuation is genuinely attractive at P/E 11.87x and forward P/E 10.49x with P/B of 2.12x — not paying a premium here
Asset base growing healthily from 27,944 Cr (FY22) to 40,967 Cr (FY25) — loan book expansion is being funded with maintained equity ratios
key_risks: Promoter is Canara Bank (PSU) at only 29.99% — PSU governance is inherently weaker; promoter has no personal wealth at stake, and strategic alignment with minority shareholders is unpredictable
Finance costs growing at 29.3% CAGR vs revenue CAGR of 18.8% — cost of funds is rising faster than lending income, compressing net interest margin
Only 2 out of 4 years of positive OCF — a lender with inconsistent operating cash conversion is a concern, even accounting for loan disbursement timing
red_flags: Promoter holding at 29.99% — the lowest of all five stocks reviewed; well below my 55% floor
PSU bank as promoter: Canara Bank's priorities (government mandates, priority sector lending) may not align with maximising Can Fin's franchise value
Finance cost CAGR of 29.3% is structurally dangerous if rate environment stays elevated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Housing finance is a business I can understand — simple model, long-duration assets, predictable demand driven by India's urban housing deficit. Can Fin Homes has historically maintained good asset quality and has a lean cost structure. The 22% PAT CAGR over FY22-25 and ROE of 16.9% are respectable, and the P/E of 11.87x prices in reasonable pessimism for the sector.

However, what concerns me most is the promoter structure. Canara Bank at 29.99% is a PSU, which means the entity with the largest stake is accountable to the government rather than to shareholders' wealth creation. This is structurally different from a founder-promoter where personal wealth is tied to the stock. The rapid rise in finance costs (2,485 Cr in FY25 vs 1,150 Cr in FY22) also suggests NIM compression that the headline PAT growth may be masking via loan book expansion. I would require a stronger franchise moat and promoter quality before making this a core holding.
